swap.evidence: Swapped into a community-hall room booking site and a council allotment waiting-list form: the masthead (icon + name in bold body text), the off-white ground with white bordered cards, the green filled button, the icon-tile card grid, the summary boxes and the footer line all survive unchanged; only the wrench glyph and the copy would change. Bound to this product: the calendar's 'Open' session markers and the Wednesday/Saturday session cards, plus the deposit lines. With the name hidden, a reader could tell it is a lending/booking tool only from the copy, not from any visual element.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community/municipal booking service: GOV.UK-like single sans, white/off-white ground, one green or blue accent, bordered cards, error summary at top, generic icons in place of photos. Predicted opposite: a warm, handmade, craft-paper 'neighbourhood' look. The rendered first viewport (find/default/1280-light) matches the default on every identity-carrying element: green accent, plain sans, bordered card grid with generic icon tiles, error summary pattern (confirm/errors).

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'a volunteer-run seed library where members reserve seed packets for collection at Saturday sessions'. Predicted choices: green accent, off-white ground, card grid with a generic leaf icon per item, search + filter bar, availability chips, calendar for collection day, check-and-confirm page. Overlap is near total; only the glyph would change. The calendar-with-session-days would also be produced, so it is product-shaped but not unique to this brief.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: The sealed section contained zero hits, so nothing anchored or changed either verdict. Most of my items are judgement-only or state/composition issues outside the detectors' reach; the zero count should not be read as a clean craft bill.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same placeholder wrench tile instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical pale-green square with the same wrench outline where an image would be. It carries no information and reads as an unfilled image slot.
findings.impact: Members choosing between similar tools (two 18 V drills, two tile cutters) get no visual help to recognise the item, and the page is likely to look unfinished; the 'neighbourly' attribute loses its best lever, the library's real tools.

evidence.detail: ten identical icon tiles in the card grid

findings.recommendation: Decide what each card's image slot is for: show the actual tool (the library owns one of each) or drop the slot so the card is text-led; do not keep a stand-in.

findings.title: Tool names truncated on phones so the two drills read the same
findings.description: At 375 px the card titles are cut with an ellipsis; both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', hiding the distinguishing 'two batteries' / 'one battery'.
findings.impact: On the primary device the deciding detail of the tool name is hidden, so members may open the wrong tool.
findings.recommendation: Let tool names wrap at narrow widths; decide how the card gives space to the name rather than to the image slot.

findings.title: Search and filter moved below all ten tools on phones
findings.description: At 375 px the 'Search tools' field, Search button and filter toggle appear after the full card list, just above Opening times; at 1280 they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Members with a tool in mind on a phone are likely to scroll past ten cards before finding the search, and the order differs from the desktop page.
findings.recommendation: Keep the search where the find job starts at every width.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions listed newest-first and include days before the chosen pick-up day
findings.description: The basket lists Wed 28 Oct first and Sat 10 Oct last, while the tool line above says 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'; sessions on 10 and 14 Oct are offered too.
findings.impact: Members are likely to scan against calendar order and may pick a session that contradicts the day they chose; this undercuts 'careful'.
findings.recommendation: Decide the session order from the member's chosen pick-up day and calendar order.

findings.title: Session radio cards wrap into a ragged one-plus-five grid
findings.description: At 1280 the first session card spans the full width and five narrow cards follow, each wrapping to three lines; at 768 a 3+3 grid has uneven card heights.
findings.impact: The odd first card reads as more important than the others and the cramped wraps slow scanning of dates and times.
findings.recommendation: Choose one layout for the session list that gives every option the same weight and lets each date-and-time read on one line where width allows.

findings.title: Filter panel uses an unthemed native date input in yyyy/mm/dd and a default select
findings.description: The 'Available from' date field shows 'yyyy/mm/dd' with a native calendar glyph; the Category select is a browser default; the two controls sit on different baselines.
findings.impact: The format conflicts with the product's en-GB 'Saturday 17 October' dates, may confuse members, and makes the panel look unfinished next to the themed controls elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Decide how dates are entered and displayed in line with the product's date format and the existing calendar component, and align the filter controls.

findings.title: No-results search shows the full tool list without an empty-state message
findings.description: With 'sewing machine' in the search box, the page still shows all ten tools under 'Tools' and no message says nothing matched.
findings.impact: Members may think the library has the item or that search did nothing.

evidence.detail: query shown, full list rendered, no empty message

findings.recommendation: Design the empty result: say nothing matched, and offer the way back to all tools or the desk.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar has no month or year label
findings.description: The calendar grid starts at Fr 9 and runs to Th 29 with weekday headers only; no 'October 2026' heading or month navigation is visible.
findings.impact: Members may be unsure which month they are choosing in, especially near a month boundary.

evidence.detail: calendar region y 750-1075 shows weekday headers only

findings.recommendation: Give the calendar a visible month heading.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar's button sits off the content column
findings.description: The 'Reserve this tool' button in the bottom bar ends at about x=1264 while the content column ends at 1184, so it does not line up with the calendar or anything above it.
findings.impact: The page's primary action floats away from the grid at wide widths, a visible alignment lapse on the critical journey.
findings.recommendation: Align the action bar's content to the page's content width.

findings.title: Tool details split into two lists with different label column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x≈224 while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x≈180, under one 'Details' heading.
findings.impact: The jagged value column makes the spec table harder to scan and looks careless, against 'careful, not fussy'.
findings.recommendation: Treat the details as one list with one label column.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the chip ground on green availability badges only
findings.description: In dark mode the 'Available from' badges in green have no visible chip background, while the grey 'later' badges keep theirs, so the two badge variants no longer share a shape.
findings.impact: The badge reads as two different components in the theme many members use, weakening the availability signal's consistency.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge so both variants keep one shape, distinguished by colour role.

findings.title: 'Your name' field keeps a default border in the error state
findings.description: On confirm with errors, the membership and mobile inputs get red borders but the 'Your name' input, also in error, keeps a dark default border.
findings.impact: Inconsistent error marking may make members miss one of the fields to fix.
findings.recommendation: Apply the error treatment to every field in error.

findings.title: Header still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: The done page confirms reservation FT-4471 while the navigation still reads 'Basket (1)'.
findings.impact: Members may wonder whether the reservation went through or whether an item is still pending.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the basket shows once a reservation is made.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in body type; no signature on any surface
findings.description: The masthead is a small wrench glyph and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type; nothing on any screen comes from the library's world (the membership card, the room, the tools). The Open-day calendar is the only product-shaped device and it is styled as a default grid.
findings.impact: The pages are likely to read as a generic booking template, and the 'neighbourly' attribute is carried only by copy.
findings.recommendation: Decide the identity floor for Operate surfaces: the name as a designed mark and one signature drawn from the library's own mechanism (sessions, the membership card), carried quietly across all five pages.

findings.title: Footer ends above an empty grey band on short pages
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280 the white footer band stops mid-viewport and a flat grey band fills the rest.
findings.impact: The page looks unfinished at desktop widths.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages fill the viewport so the footer closes the page.

findings.title: Navigation labels wrap onto two lines on phones
findings.description: At 375 px 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)' and 'Opening / times' each break across two lines under the masthead.
findings.impact: On the main device the nav looks broken and the basket count separates from its label.
findings.recommendation: Decide a phone navigation pattern in which each label stays on one line.

strengths: Plain, concrete volunteer voice: deposit, sessions and what to bring are stated on every relevant page.
The Open-day calendar (with a dot on phones) makes the part-time desk visible at the moment of choice.
Composed dark theme with the same roles, and a linked error summary pattern on basket and confirm.
keep: Keep the one-accent, one-filled-button discipline and the session-aware calendar; fix finish and identity without adding ornament.
not_assessable: Toast fade, button hover and focus behaviour, listbox shadow and motion cannot be judged from stills. The sticky bar's overlap of the calendar may be partly a full-page-capture artefact.
